A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D-SEC/Gandalf study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. V1 Appendices G–H correspond to v3 Appendices H–I, following insertion of the GPT-4o experiment.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gandalf-RCT data collection and experiments on security, benign-user utility, defense aggregation, adaptive defenses, and attack categories.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and adds experiments replaying existing prompts against GPT-4o in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The D-SEC framework, defense components, aggregation optimization, and session-blocking procedure are retained. Appendix A's operational prompts and defense configurations remain substantively unchanged; GPT-4o is an additional experimental configuration.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gandalf-RCT's general, summarization, and topic setups, plus BasicUser and BorderlineUser. The added GPT-4o experiment reuses existing prompts and tasks rather than introducing another dataset, population, or application domain.

E2.justification: The evaluated defense alternatives and aggregation comparators remain unchanged. GPT-4o is an additional target-model configuration, not a new competing defense. Newly cited research is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds retrospective GPT-4o evaluation, including a 2,400-prompt defense-overlap analysis, rather than fresh adaptive gameplay. Section 3.1.1 also revises reported sessions/users from 36,239/15,402 to 36,286/15,448, although Appendix B retains the earlier counts; this does not establish recollection or rerunning of the original experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a target-model sensitivity check and examines failures of substring-based refusal detection on GPT-4o. Existing analyses of domain restrictions, defense overlap, blocking thresholds, accidental disclosures, and attack categories remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals for false-positive rates and attack-category results. V3 extends this reporting to GPT-4o, displaying upper endpoints in Table S.12, without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, repeated-run count, or seed information.

E6.justification: Table S.10 revises developer utilities: at lambda = 0.5, the or/and/optimal values change from 0.73/0.55/0.76 to 0.75/0.57/0.79. Appendix G adds GPT-4o overlap and utility results, including 985/2,400 responses classified as undetected, explicitly distinguished from successful password extraction. Existing charts and principal findings are retained.

T1.justification: V3 explicitly assumes that security and utility have been transformed to comparable units before combination in the objective (footnote 5). The metric definitions, optimization equations, Proposition E.1, and appendix derivations otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The four principal contributions remain D-SEC, the Gandalf attack dataset, evidence of security–utility trade-offs, and support for domain restriction, defense aggregation, and adaptive defenses. The abstract and discussion retain these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly explains that replay loses adaptive interactions and that unblocked GPT-4o responses need not disclose passwords, motivating stronger semantic detection. Section 5 makes the password-extraction boundary more explicit, building on v1's existing generalizability caveat.

D1.justification: V3 specifies the added gpt-4o-2024-11-20 checkpoint and replay provenance, and newly documents a responsible-use dataset license. Existing implementation details and resource locations are retained; the code link moves from the abstract to Appendix I.

R1.justification: V3 adds Sharma et al. (2025), positioning its utility analysis beyond over-refusals, and Verma et al. (2024) when specifying attacker capabilities. The broader research positioning is retained; bibliographic corrections do not constitute additional research changes.

P1.justification: V3 condenses several method and experiment descriptions, folds the prompt-attack primer into Section 2, and adds an Impact Statement. Appendix insertion and renumbering preserve the existing narrative and appendix content rather than substantially reorganizing the argument.

P2.justification: V3 adopts ICML typesetting throughout, changing the title block, abstract placement, typography, running headers, and arrangement of text and displays. Existing figures are retained but repositioned, including Figures 6 and S.6. Appendix G adds a Venn diagram and two tables.

improvement.justification: The qualified GPT-4o extension provides useful evidence about model sensitivity and refusal-measurement limitations. Revised Table S.10 security values also agree with the retained Figure 5 overlap counts. These are limited gains: the extension does not validate adaptive GPT-4o gameplay, v3 introduces conflicting session/user totals between Section 3.1.1 and Appendix B, and Table S.12 labels false-positive percentages as SCR. Overall, the added evidence and improved numerical consistency modestly strengthen the paper.
